docs.title: NOMAD ML Workflows
docs.text: nomad-ml-workflows helps you turn NOMAD entries into reusable datasets and describe machine learning models alongside their artifacts, training metadata, and evaluations.

docs.title: Choose an export action
docs.text:
Action Use it for Output Export Entries Complete archives or selected archive paths from this deployment JSON, CSV, or a Parquet dataset in a staging project/upload Export Forces Atomic structures with selected energies, forces, and stresses; shown as Export MLIP Data Action in the GUI Extended XYZ or an ASE database in a staging project/upload Export Remote Entries Entries from configured Oases, optionally including this deployment One export per target in S3, optionally copied into a staging project/upload on the deployment that starts the action

Each action runs independently. They share permission-scoped search and archive extraction, with Export Entries providing the foundation. Read the export explanation for selection, formats, manifests, and counts.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow the short Export Entries tutorial to save up to ten visible entries as JSON in a ZIP, using either the GUI or a Python REST client. Use the action chooser for task-specific guides.

Administrators can follow installation and configuration to enable the plugin, set limits and action access, and configure remote targets and storage.

docs.title: Describe models and datasets
docs.text: The Schema explanation introduces the ML Model and Dataset schemas. Describe model versions, libraries, files, training datasets, and evaluation metrics in an MLModel entry. Use Dataset to describe data through NOMAD references, files, or URLs.

docs.title: Export functionality
docs.text: The three export actions share a sequence: search entries using the initiating user's permissions, record the selected entry IDs in a manifest, read their archives, write the requested format, and publish the artifacts. Export Entries supplies this foundation; Export Forces converts archives into atomic structures, while Export Remote Entries runs extraction on selected deployments and saves each dataset to S3. You can start any action independently.

docs.title: Search selection and archive content
docs.text:
search_settings.query is a NOMAD search query encoded as JSON text, for example '{"entry_type": "ELNSample"}' in a JSON input file. You can write the query yourself. Or you can use a search app to make a selection and copy the query object from View API Call; this is the recommened way. Make sure to only copy the query object rather than the whole API request body. The tutorial shows where to use it. The query determines which entries match.

search_settings.owner determines the ownership scope:

Value Eligible entries visible All entries visible to the initiating user; the default public Public entries user The user's entries shared The user's entries and entries shared with them staging The user's and shared unpublished entries

max_entries is a positive selection limit. Its default is the smaller of 1,000 and the configured deployment cap. The action selects up to the applicable limit from the search results; it does not sample randomly.

For Export Entries and Export Remote Entries, search_settings.required controls what is read from each selected archive. An empty list requests the complete archive. Both include and exclude directives use dot-separated section or quantity paths, such as results.method.

  • type: include selects a path. Set resolve_references: true to include data reached through references below it, subject to access permissions.
  • type: exclude removes a path. An exclude-only list starts from the complete archive and removes the specified paths.

Choosing a path does not filter out entries where that path is absent; use the search query to require matching content. See the action form inputs for examples.

Export Forces instead uses search_settings.properties to select energies, forces, and stresses. It adds corresponding quantity-presence conditions to its search query and reads the archive data needed by the forces exporter.

docs.title: Formats and packaging
docs.text:
Format Representation json A JSON array of records containing entry_id, upload_id, and the selected archive; preserves archive structure parquet One row per exported entry, with archive sections flattened into columns and nested quantity values preserved; written as a directory of part files (shards) sharing one schema csv Flattened archive columns; nested values are encoded as JSON text in cells extxyz / ase_db Atomic structures and selected properties, available through Export Forces

Tabular export follows the installed NOMAD metainfo definitions. Data without a corresponding current schema definition may be omitted or an entry may be skipped; consult the action logs when counts differ.

export_settings.create_zip_archive defaults to true. Export Entries and Export Forces put a ZIP into the destination upload's raw files on the deployment where you start the action. With false, they create a subdirectory containing the same artifacts. Remote export uses an S3 object for ZIP output or an S3 prefix for directory output. In that action, local means the initiating deployment; optional copying saves the remote datasets into an upload on that deployment.

docs.title: Manifest, metadata, and counts
docs.text:
Every successful export includes selected_entries.json, an ordered list of selected entry_id/upload_id pairs, and metadata.json. Metadata contains a note, a schema, and a data object with the original inputs, search timestamps, deployment host, package versions, and these fields:

Field under data Meaning num_entries_available Total search matches before applying the selection limit num_entries_selected Entries recorded in the manifest after applying the limit num_entries_exported Exported archive records or tabular rows for Export Entries; Export Forces records the selected manifest count, which is not a count of atomic configurations reached_max_entries_limit Whether the total matches exceeded the selection limit error_info Extraction error information, when recorded

The manifest records selection, not a guarantee that every archive could be read or converted. Check counts and logs before using a dataset. A search with zero matches still produces metadata and an empty manifest, but no data artifact. This applies to the forces export and each remote extraction as well.

Remote export returns per-target results, where counts are summed across targets.

docs.title: Models and datasets
docs.text: Exports produce files that you can use in downstream training. The separate MLModel and Dataset schemas describe model artifacts and their provenance. Running an export does not automatically create an MLModel or Dataset entry, train a model, or compute evaluation metrics.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
Schemas under development

These schemas are under development and can change without notice.

The plugin provides schemas for recording machine learning models and the datasets used to train or evaluate them.

docs.title: ML Model
docs.text: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.model.MLModel describes a machine learning model independently of its implementation library and artifact format. It is a NOMAD schema that can be used as an entry's data section and edited in the ELN. It records the model and its provenance; it does not load model weights, run training, or calculate evaluation scores.

docs.title: Model identity and implementation
docs.text:
Alongside the inherited Entity metadata, such as name, MLModel provides:

Field Meaning architecture Architecture or model family, such as resnet or U-Net model_version Your version identifier for this model license License under which the model is available tasks List of intended tasks tags Free-form discovery labels libraries Repeatable records, each with name and version

The task and library editors offer suggestions from the Hugging Face model-tag catalog. These suggestions are optional UI metadata: a temporary catalog/network failure leaves them empty without preventing the schema from loading. Recording a model does not require uploading it to Hugging Face.

docs.title: Artifacts and normalization
docs.text:
artifacts is repeatable, so one model can refer to multiple files, such as weights and a separate model representation. Each artifact has model_file (a path relative to the upload's raw files), format, file_size in bytes, and checksum.

During normalization, an existing artifact file supplies its size, replacing any previously recorded file_size. If format is missing, the final file extension supplies it in lowercase: weights.PT yields pt. An explicitly supplied format is preserved. A missing file causes a warning and does not supply size or format.

Checksums are supplied metadata: normalization does not calculate or verify them. Record the algorithm with the value, for example using a sha256: prefix. Evaluation results are also supplied metadata and are not recomputed.

docs.title: Training and evaluation
docs.text:
The single training subsection records epochs, batch_size, a dataset reference, and dataset_split (for example, train). Its optional optimizer subsection records name and learning_rate.

evaluations is repeatable. Each record holds one metric_name/metric_value pair, a dataset reference, and a dataset_split, such as test. Use separate records for different metrics, datasets, or splits, and make metric names precise enough to explain their scale and units.

Training and evaluation references point to a Dataset section. The dataset_split field labels the portion used without creating or enforcing that split.

docs.title: Model archive example
docs.text:
Save the following as model.archive.yaml in a NOMAD upload with the model schema enabled:

data:
  m_def: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.model.MLModel
  name: Example image classifier
  architecture: resnet
  model_version: "1.0"
  license: MIT
  tasks:
    - image-classification
  tags:
    - example
  libraries:
    - name: pytorch
      version: "2.5"
  artifacts:
    - model_file: models/weights.pt
      format: pytorch-state-dict
  training:
    epochs: 20
    batch_size: 32
    dataset_split: train
    optimizer:
      name: Adam
      learning_rate: 0.001
  evaluations:
    - metric_name: Accuracy (fraction)
      metric_value: 0.91
      dataset_split: test

Upload your actual weights at models/weights.pt to let normalization record their size. The explicit format remains pytorch-state-dict. Supply an actual checksum if available; the example leaves it unset. The evaluation value illustrates manually recorded metadata.

To connect provenance, create a Dataset entry and use its reference in training.dataset and each applicable evaluations[].dataset field through the reference editor.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.dataset.Dataset describes a dataset through NOMAD archive references, raw files, external URLs, or a combination of these sources. Like MLModel, it can be used as an entry's data section.

Field Meaning references References to NOMAD archive sections or entries comprising the dataset files Paths relative to the dataset upload's raw files urls URLs of externally hosted dataset resources

An export action produces files, which you can describe in a Dataset entry yourself. Reference that entry from a model's training and evaluation records to connect their provenance.

docs.title: Dataset archive example
docs.text:
Save this as dataset.archive.yaml in an upload with the Dataset schema enabled:

data:
  m_def: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.dataset.Dataset
  name: Classifier data
  files:
    - datasets/images.zip

Replace this raw-file path with your dataset's location in its upload. Use references for NOMAD archive sections or urls for externally hosted data when those better describe your dataset.

docs.title: Set up development
docs.text:
We recommend using uv to manage Python environments and dependencies, with Python 3.10 or newer. Clone the repository and install the development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-ml-workflows.git
cd nomad-ml-workflows
uv sync --python 3.12 --extra dev
. .venv/bin/activate

Run the commands below from the plugin repository root.

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
Run the full test suite:

uv run pytest tests/

To run a subset, pass a test directory or file:

uv run pytest tests/actions/export_entries/
uv run pytest tests/actions/export_entries/test_models.py

Use -k EXPRESSION to select tests by name and -v for verbose output.

docs.title: Check code and documentation
docs.text:
Run linting and formatting checks with Ruff:

uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format . --check

To apply automatic formatting, run uv run ruff format ..

Markdown linting requires Node.js 22 or newer and npm/npx:

uv run poe markdown-lint

Add --fix to apply automatic Markdown fixes: uv run poe markdown-lint --fix.

docs.title: Preview documentation
docs.text:
Serve the documentation locally:

uv run mkdocs serve

Before submitting documentation changes, check that the site builds without warnings:

uv run mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Export entries
docs.text: Use Export Entries Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries) to save archives from the deployment where you start the action as JSON, CSV, or Parquet. The tutorial demonstrates the GUI and a Python REST submission.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need access to the action and source entries, a writable staging project/upload for the output, and a running CPU action worker. Administrators can follow installation and configuration.

docs.title: Select entries and content
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Run action → Export Entries Action and set Destination project ID to your staging upload ID.
  2. Choose the ownership scope, a positive maximum entry count, and the search query. Enter the query as JSON text.
  3. Leave Archive required paths empty for full archives, or add include/exclude directives. Enable reference resolution on included paths where needed.
  4. Select json, parquet, or csv, choose ZIP or directory output, and run the action.

docs.title: Action form inputs
Retrieve and inspect the export
docs.text:
Monitor the action instance's status and logs. After success, its exported_dir_path gives the ZIP filename or directory path relative to the destination upload's raw files; workflow_duration reports elapsed seconds. Open the project's files to download it.

Artifact Contents data.json JSON array of records containing entry_id, upload_id, and the selected archive data.csv Flattened columns, with nested values as JSON text data.parquet/part-NNNNN.parquet Parquet parts sharing a schema; nested quantity values are preserved selected_entries.json Selected entry_id/upload_id pairs metadata.json Inputs, counts, timing, deployment/package versions, and a JSON schema

Only the selected data format is produced. Read the whole extracted Parquet directory with PyArrow:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

table = pq.read_table('data.parquet')

Compare num_entries_available, num_entries_selected, and num_entries_exported under metadata's data object. The manifest describes selection; archive-read or flattening failures may reduce the exported count. Inspect logs for skipped entries. A zero-match export contains metadata and an empty manifest, with no data artifact. See manifest and count semantics.

docs.title: Export energies, forces, and stresses
docs.text:
Use Export MLIP Data Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces) to export atomic structures and selected properties for machine learning interatomic potentials. Its formats are Extended XYZ (extxyz) and ASE database (ase_db).

Currently only DFT entries are supported.

magmoms are currently only added for VASP DFT entries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need access to the action and compatible calculation archives, a writable staging project/upload, and a running CPU action worker with the cpu-action dependencies installed, including nomad-forces-export. See administrator setup.

docs.title: Configure and run
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Run action → Export MLIP Data Action and set the destination staging upload ID.
  2. Choose an ownership scope and maximum entry count. Keep or adapt the prefilled calculation query for your source data.
{ 
  "results.method.method_name:any": [ "DFT" ],   
  "quantities:all": 
    [ "run.calculation", 
      "run.system" ] 
}
  1. Under Properties, select energies, forces, and/or stresses. The underlying field names are exactly energies, forces, and stresses; each defaults to false.
  2. Choose extxyz and/or ase_db, select ZIP or directory output, and run the action.
  3. Inspect status, logs, and results, then download the output from the destination project's files using exported_dir_path.

The action adds quantity-presence conditions for the selected properties to the query (run.calculation.energy.total_t0.value, run.calculation.forces.total.value, and run.calculation.stress.total.value). Use archives supported by nomad-forces-export; general ELN entries need not contain compatible structures or calculation data.

docs.title: Example input
docs.text:
This input requests energy and force data from up to 100 public matching entries. {} adds no user filters; the action still adds the selected property requirements. For a narrower dataset, use a query copied from a search app's View API Call dialog.

{
  "upload_id": "YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID",
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "public",
    "max_entries": 100,
    "query": "{}",
    "properties": {
      "energies": true,
      "forces": true,
      "stresses": false
    }
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "extxyz",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

For REST, omit user_id and send the input under data to this action's start endpoint. query is JSON text. Ownership scopes and limits follow the shared selection rules. Forces uses properties instead of an archive required list; its extractor chooses the archive content needed for atomic data.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
The ZIP or directory contains data.xyz for Extended XYZ or data.db for an ASE database, plus selected_entries.json and metadata.json. Set file_format to ase_db for database output, or create_zip_archive to false for a directory. The result also reports workflow_duration.

Metadata records source selection, inputs, versions, and timing.

num_entries_exported is set to the number of entries that were processed; it does not measure the number of exported atomic configurations. An entry can contain multiple configurations, and conversion may skip unsupported frames. The archive filtering checks for relevant properties being present before adding a entry to the count, however due to errors within the archive data there might be no usable frames in that entry.

num_frames_exported gives the actual total number of frames exported acroos all the entries.

Inspect logs and the generated atomic dataset to assess its contents.

A zero-match run produces an empty manifest and metadata without data.xyz or data.db. See the shared export explanation for packaging and provenance.

docs.title: Export remote entries
docs.text:
Use Export Remote Entries Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries) to run the same archive extraction on configured Oases over Temporal Nexus.

In this guide, local means the current NOMAD deployment from which you start the action, also called the initiating deployment. The local target extracts entries from that deployment; other targets extract entries from remote deployments. Each target writes its own export to S3. You can also copy successful exports into a staging upload on the initiating deployment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
An administrator must configure Nexus endpoints, action access, storage, and CPU workers on participating deployments; see remote export setup. The initiating user's ID is forwarded to remote extraction, which applies that user's permissions there. Participating deployments must recognize that identity, trust the Nexus callers, and configure matching payload encryption keys.

S3 storage must be accessible to the workers that write exports. Copying datasets back also requires storage access for the initiating deployment's worker and a writable staging upload there. For ZIP copy-back, configure the same bucket name on the initiating and receiving deployments; the current copy implementation uses the initiating bucket when parsing presigned URLs. The staging upload is needed only when save_to_upload is true.

Action submission through the GUI and HTTP API defaults to users: [admin]; administrators must configure the intended user IDs or groups. Incoming Nexus calls do not recheck the receiver's action users or groups lists, so access to the receiving endpoint must be restricted to trusted callers.

docs.title: Choose targets and run
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Run action → Export Remote Entries Action.
  2. Choose one or more Target Oases. local runs extraction on the initiating deployment; other values are administrator-configured Nexus target keys.
  3. Set search options, including ownership scope, maximum entries, query JSON text, and optional archive include/exclude directives. The selection limit applies separately to each target.
  4. Select json, csv, or parquet and ZIP or directory output.
  5. Leave Save dataset to upload disabled for S3-only output, or enable it and provide the destination staging upload ID.
  6. Run the action, then inspect every target's result.

docs.title: Example input
docs.text:
With the administrator's oasis-b target configured and deployment-managed storage (s3_mode: env), this input exports up to ten visible entries from each of the initiating deployment (local) and the remote oasis-b deployment:

{
  "target_oases": ["local", "oasis-b"],
  "save_to_upload": false,
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "visible",
    "max_entries": 10,
    "query": "{}",
    "required": []
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "json",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

Use the keys supplied by your administrator. To search only remote data, omit local from target_oases. To copy each successful dataset to an upload on the initiating deployment, set save_to_upload to true and add upload_id. Each target remains a separate export; the action does not merge datasets.

For REST, omit user_id and submit this input under data. Search query text and archive include/exclude directives follow Export Entries. Remote export does not produce forces formats.

docs.title: Storage options
docs.text:
In the default env mode, the worker resolves storage from deployment configuration and environment variables, and the form hides storage_settings. Supplied storage settings are replaced by deployment-managed values on a deployment running in this mode.

If the administrator enables s3_mode: workflow_input, add this storage_settings object to the action input:

{
  "storage_settings": {
    "storage_type": "s3",
    "bucket": "ml-datasets",
    "prefix": "exports",
    "region": "eu-central-1"
  }
}

This fragment supplements the complete input above. endpoint_url can select an S3-compatible service; optional access_key_id, secret_access_key, and session_token supply explicit credentials. Without explicit credentials, the S3 client can use each executing worker's configured credential chain.

Credentials in the initiating deployment's resolved storage settings are serialized into workflow payloads and forwarded to every selected Nexus receiver. This includes input credentials in workflow_input mode and credentials resolved from plugin configuration or access-key environment variables in env mode. A receiver in env mode still receives these values before replacing them with its own storage settings. Restrict receivers and access to workers and Temporal histories accordingly. Worker role or profile credentials resolved later by boto3 are not added to the workflow payload by this plugin; see storage configuration.

A remote deployment in env mode resolves its own storage even when the caller supplies settings; the initiating deployment's worker must be able to read that storage if copying into its upload is requested.

docs.title: Inspect the results
docs.text:
Result field Meaning results Mapping from each target key to its execution summary results.<target>.status SUCCESS or FAILED results.<target>.is_remote Whether the target used Nexus results.<target>.num_entries_exported Exported count for that target results.<target>.remote_uri Download URL or S3 URI on success; use only after checking status results.<target>.error_message Target failure details, when present total_entries_exported Sum across targets, without deduplication remote_uri Primary URI, preferring output from the initiating deployment's local target; inspect per-target results for usable locations workflow_duration Total elapsed seconds

A remote target can report FAILED while other targets succeed and the parent workflow completes. A failure of the local target can fail the parent workflow. Copying into an upload on the initiating deployment is part of each target's execution and can fail after its S3 output was written; inspect logs as well as results.

Successful S3 ZIPs or prefixes contain the same data artifact, manifest, and metadata as Export Entries. ZIP output normally returns a presigned download URL with a requested lifetime of two days (subject to credential expiry), falling back to an s3:// URI if signing fails. Directory output returns an s3:// prefix. Zero-match targets still write metadata and an empty manifest, without a data artifact. If copying was requested, find the copied ZIPs or directories in the destination project's files on the initiating deployment. The action returns storage locations rather than upload paths.

docs.title: Install and configure the plugin
docs.text: This guide covers installing and configuring the plugin in an existing NOMAD environment. For Temporal and CPU action-worker setup, follow Enabling NOMAD Actions in the distribution template.

docs.title: NOMAD deployment
docs.text:
The plugin requires nomad-lab>=2.0.0. Add it to your distribution following the NOMAD Oasis plugin configuration guide. Include the cpu-action extra for export dependencies when adding the plugin to the deployment's pyproject.toml:

[project]
dependencies = [
  ...
  "nomad-ml-workflows[cpu-action]",
]

The extra supplies PyArrow for tabular output, boto3 for S3, and nomad-forces-export for atomic data. The base installation provides the schema packages and action registration. Configure the plugin in your deployment's nomad.yaml as described below.

docs.title: NOMAD distro dev
docs.text:
Use nomad-distro-dev for an integrated development installation. Follow its setup instructions to add this plugin under packages/nomad-ml-workflows and register nomad-ml-workflows[cpu-action] as a workspace dependency. Apply the plugin settings below in the workspace's root nomad.yaml.

For plugin tests, linting, and documentation previews, see Contribute to this plugin.

docs.title: Enable entry points
docs.text:
The plugin registers these entry points:

Entry point Purpose nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries Archive export from this deployment nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces Atomic structures and properties nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries Nexus and S3 export nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages:dataset_schema Dataset schema nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages:model_schema ML model schema

Ensure the required entry points are included in your deployment's plugin selection and are not excluded. Configure action options under plugins.entry_points.options as below. Confirm the actions are offered by the GUI or authenticated GET /actions/schemas relative to the deployment's API base URL.

docs.title: Set limits and action access
docs.text:
Merge this example into the existing nomad.yaml, replacing the example user and group IDs:

plugins:
  entry_points:
    options:
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries:
        max_entries_export_limit: 100000
        read_archives_timeout: 7200
        write_tabular_timeout: 7200
        max_write_buffer_size_bytes: 67108864
        max_write_buffer_size_rows: 1024
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces:
        max_entries_export_limit: 100000
        export_archives_timeout: 10800
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]

Limits must be positive; 0 does not mean unlimited. The shared manifest activity uses the Export Entries cap, including for forces and remote exports. Forces also validates its input against its own cap; keep the two caps aligned when you want the same limit. A remote search applies the executing deployment's cap separately for each target.

Timeouts are in seconds. The two tabular buffer limits control buffered rows and encoded input bytes, not a hard process-memory ceiling; one oversized row can exceed the byte target.

users and groups contain NOMAD IDs and restrict action submission through the GUI and HTTP API. A user is allowed if their ID is listed or they belong to a listed group. Empty or unset restrictions allow authenticated users to start the action. Entry permissions still apply to searches. Remote export defaults to users: [admin]; replace it with intended IDs, or set users: [] and a nonempty groups list for group-only access.

docs.title: Configure remote export
docs.text:
Here, local means the initiating deployment: the current NOMAD deployment from which the action is started. Its local target searches that deployment, and optional upload copying saves datasets there.

Enable the remote action and its Nexus handler on the receiving deployment as well as the initiating one. Use Nexus endpoints already available in your deployment. The receiving deployment must recognize the forwarded initiating user's ID.

docs.title: Configure Nexus trust and payload encryption
docs.text:
Restrict access to the receiving Nexus endpoint to trusted initiating deployments using your Temporal authentication and authorization setup. Incoming Nexus calls start the export workflow directly and do not recheck the receiving action's users or groups lists. The receiver trusts the caller to forward the authenticated user's ID; extraction then applies that identity's entry permissions. Configuring a receiver's action allowlists does not restrict incoming Nexus calls.

Configure the same Temporal payload encryption key and key ID in the API and CPU worker environments of all participating deployments. Merge this into each deployment's existing nomad.yaml, replacing the placeholder with the same securely supplied secret of at least 32 characters:

temporal:
  payload_codec_key: "<shared-secret-at-least-32-characters>"
  payload_codec_key_id: nomad-export-federation

Keep each deployment's services.api_secret separate. Without an explicit payload key, production clients encrypt using their own API secret, so independently configured deployments cannot decode each other's Nexus payloads. Development clients otherwise leave payloads unencrypted; configure the shared key explicitly when communicating with encrypted peers.

docs.title: Configure targets and S3
docs.text:
Merge this configuration on the initiating deployment:

plugins:
  entry_points:
    options:
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries:
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]
        local_display_name: Local Oasis
        nexus_endpoints:
          oasis-b:
            display_name: Oasis B
            endpoint: oasis-b
        s3_mode: env
        s3_bucket: ml-datasets
        s3_prefix: exports
        s3_region: eu-central-1

Use the same name for the mapping key (oasis-b), the endpoint value, and the registered Nexus endpoint. Current dispatch uses the selected mapping key as the endpoint name. local is reserved for execution on the initiating deployment. The display name is only a GUI label.

The default s3_mode: env resolves storage on each executing deployment. Set an accessible bucket and credentials on each deployment; configuring the initiating worker alone does not configure a receiver. For optional copying back to an upload on the initiating deployment, its worker must also be able to read the receiver's storage, using a compatible endpoint and credentials.

For ZIP copy-back, configure the same bucket name on the initiating and receiving deployments. ZIP exports normally return a presigned URL, and the current copy implementation parses that URL using the initiating deployment's configured bucket. Read access to a different receiver bucket alone is insufficient. Directory exports return an s3:// URI that preserves the receiver's bucket name, so those buckets can differ if the initiating worker has the required storage access.

Entry point option Environment fallback s3_bucket S3_BUCKET, AWS_S3_BUCKET, AWS_BUCKET s3_prefix S3_PREFIX, AWS_S3_PREFIX s3_endpoint_url S3_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL s3_region S3_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_REGION s3_access_key_id S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID s3_secret_access_key S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY s3_session_token S3_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN

Entry point values take precedence over the fallbacks, which are checked in the listed order. Set s3_endpoint_url for an S3-compatible service. Workers need permission to write export objects; copying ZIPs requires object reads, and copying directories also requires listing the export prefix.

The initiating deployment forwards its resolved storage_settings, including any credential fields, to every selected Nexus receiver through Temporal payloads. These settings come from workflow input in workflow_input mode or plugin configuration and the listed environment variables in env mode. This forwarding also happens when a receiver uses s3_mode: env and replaces those settings before exporting. Only configure trusted receivers, and restrict access to workers and Temporal payloads and histories on both initiating and receiving deployments.

When explicit credential fields are unset, boto3 can resolve credentials locally through each executing worker's configured role or profile. Credentials resolved later by boto3 are not added to the workflow payload by this plugin. Setting the listed access-key environment variables populates the credential fields and therefore forwards those values to receivers.

Alternatively, set s3_mode: workflow_input to show and require storage_settings in the action form. Configure participating receivers the same way if they should use the caller's supplied settings. A receiver in env mode replaces them with its own deployment settings. See the remote guide for an input example.

docs.title: Verify the deployment
docs.text: Run the small Export Entries tutorial, check the action instance completes, and inspect the ZIP in its destination upload. For remote setup, start with a single configured target and a small limit, check its per-target status and storage location, then enable copying into an upload on the initiating deployment if needed. Search and export counts are explained in the export overview.

docs.title: Choose an export action
docs.text:
Sign in to a deployment with the plugin enabled and an active CPU action worker. For output saved to NOMAD, create or choose a writable staging project/upload and copy its ID. Source entries may belong to other uploads, provided you can read them.

Your task Guide GUI action name Export archives or selected paths from this deployment as JSON, CSV, or Parquet Export entries Export Entries Action Export atomic structures with energies, forces, or stresses Export forces Export MLIP Data Action Search configured Oases and save results in S3 Export remote entries Export Remote Entries Action

For a first export, follow the GUI and REST tutorial. All JSON action-input examples in these guides omit user_id: NOMAD injects the authenticated user's ID when starting an action through REST, including from the GUI.

Open Actions, select Run action, choose an action, complete its form, and submit it. Use the action instance page to monitor status, inspect results, and read logs. Actions available to you depend on the deployment's configured user/group access.

If an action is missing or remains waiting to execute, consult the administrator's installation guide. For format and count semantics, read the export explanation.

docs.title: Export ten perovskite solar-cell entries on NOMAD Central
docs.text: This tutorial exports up to ten entries of type PerovskiteSolarCell visible to you on NOMAD Central. The complete archives are saved as JSON in a ZIP in your destination project. Both the GUI and Python/REST instructions below run Export Entries Action with the same inputs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Open NOMAD Central's GUI selector, select Launch New GUI, and sign in with your NOMAD account. Export Entries Action is available on this installation.
  2. Open Projects, select New Project, enter a Project name such as Perovskite export, and select Create. Leave the files empty.
  3. Open the new project's overview and keep the project unpublished so the action can write the export to it.

docs.title: Use the GUI
docs.text:
Watch the screencast or follow the steps below:

Your browser does not support embedded video. Download the screencast.
  1. In the newly created project's overview, select Run action, and choose Export Entries Action.
  2. Confirm that Destination project ID is already populated with this project's ID.
  3. Under Search options, choose All entries visible to me (visible), set Maximum entries to 10, and enter {"entry_type": "PerovskiteSolarCell"} in Search query. Leave Archive required paths empty to export complete archives.
  4. Under Export options, choose json and keep Create ZIP archive enabled. Run the action.

The action searches for entries and collects their archives in the background. To follow its progress:

  1. Select Actions in the left menu to view the actions you have run, along with their project IDs and creation times. Select the most recent action's ID in the first row to open its preview.
  2. Select Open full page in the preview to follow the action's status and logs. Once it succeeds, find the relative path of the exported artifacts under exported_dir_path in Results.

Open the destination project's files and find the ZIP at that relative path (for example, export_entries_<timestamp>.zip). If the file is not visible, reload the page. Download and extract the ZIP to inspect data.json, selected_entries.json, and metadata.json.

Use a query for your data

The query above selects perovskite solar-cell entries. To choose different data, find your entries in a NOMAD search app, open View API Call, and copy only the query object. Paste that object as JSON text into Search query. When editing an input JSON file, encode the object as a string, as shown below and in the action form inputs.

docs.title: Submit the same export with Python and REST
docs.text:
You need Python with requests installed and network access to Central's API. The client does not need a local NOMAD installation or worker.

Using the same NOMAD account, open User Settings → Tokens (Central's Tokens page). Create a personal access token with a name, an expiration date, and the actions:run and actions:read scopes, then select Create token. Copy the displayed token for NOMAD_TOKEN below. Your account must have access to the source entries and write access to the destination project. For more details, see Authenticate programmatically.

Copy the ID of the project created above. Save this as export_entries_input.json, replacing YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID with that ID; REST requests require you to supply upload_id:

{
  "upload_id": "YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID",
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "visible",
    "max_entries": 10,
    "query": "{\"entry_type\": \"PerovskiteSolarCell\"}",
    "required": []
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "json",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

query is a string containing a JSON object. Here it selects entries whose entry_type is PerovskiteSolarCell within the visible ownership scope, matching the GUI example. Omit user_id; REST injects the authenticated user's ID before validating the action inputs and overwrites any supplied value.

Set Central's API base URL and your token in your shell environment, replacing the token placeholder with the value copied above:

export NOMAD_API_URL='https://nomad-lab.eu/backend/api/v1'
export NOMAD_TOKEN='YOUR_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN'

Save the following as submit_export.py and run python submit_export.py from the directory containing the input file:

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

import requests

api_url = os.environ['NOMAD_API_URL'].rstrip('/')
token = os.environ['NOMAD_TOKEN']
input_json = json.loads(Path('export_entries_input.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
action_id = 'nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries'

response = requests.post(
    f'{api_url}/actions/{action_id}/start',
    headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'},
    json={'data': input_json},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
action_instance_id = response.json()['action_instance_id']
print(action_instance_id)
print(f'https://nomad-lab.eu/actions/{action_instance_id}')

The script submits the action and prints its instance ID and Central action-page URL. It does not wait for completion. Open the printed URL to follow the status and logs, then download the ZIP from the destination project's files as described above. You can also make authenticated requests to GET /actions/{action_instance_id}/status and, after completion, GET /actions/{action_instance_id}/result, relative to the same API base URL. The result's exported_dir_path identifies the ZIP in your destination upload's raw files.

docs.title: Check the dataset
docs.text:
After completing either interface's instructions, check the export:

  1. Confirm that the action succeeded and that the ZIP is available at exported_dir_path in the destination project's files.
  2. Extract the ZIP and check for data.json, selected_entries.json, and metadata.json.
  3. Inspect data.json, a JSON array of records with entry IDs, upload IDs, and archives for the selected PerovskiteSolarCell entries. Compare the entry and upload IDs with the selected sources in selected_entries.json.
  4. In metadata.json, inspect data.num_entries_available, data.num_entries_selected, and data.num_entries_exported. With enough readable entries, ten are selected and exported. Fewer matches or skipped archives can produce fewer exported records; check the action logs for skipped entries. Matching totals and selected entries can change as Central's data changes.

If no entries match, the ZIP still contains an empty manifest and metadata, but no data.json. For selected archive paths, other formats, and directory output, continue with Export entries.
